entities.summary:
Penelope Rosemont is a visual artist, writer, publisher, and social activist who attended Lake Forest College. She has been a participant in the Surrealist Movement since 1965. With Franklin Rosemont, Bernard Marszalek, Robert Green and Tor
Faegre, she established the Chicago Surrealist Group in 1966. She was in 1964-1966 a member of the Industrial Workers of the World (IWW), commonly known as the Wobblies, and was part of the national staff of Students for a Democratic Society (SDS) in 1967-68. Her influences include Andre Breton and Guy Debord of the Situationist International, Emma Goldman and Lucy Parsons.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: As a key figure in the Chicago Surrealist Group and member of the Industrial Workers of World (IWW) and Students for a Democratic Society (SDS), Penelope Rosemont played a significant role in the American counterculture movement of the 1960s, influencing generations of artists, activists, and writers.
